subject: Tier handoff playbook: migration orchestration and rollback credits
messages:
From: Chris Moore <chris@medspec.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@medspec.ai>
Date: 2026-08-26T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot -> Prod migration ask: handoff runbook and credits

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the pilot guidance last quarter — the model latency improvements were noticeable. We're preparing to move the pilot (approx 30k tokens/day, 50 QPS peak) into production and we'd like to lock down an operational handoff plan and any protections for an early rollback.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood provide a short migration playbook (canary -> phased rollout) we can follow and share with SRE?
- For the first 90 days post-migration, would Redwood consider conditional rollback credits (in case we need to revert due to data or quality regressions)?
- Any constraints on feature bundles or tier swaps during the canary window?

Attaching an internal spec and our expected QPS/retention profile. Happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Chris
Head of Platform
MedSpec Analytics

Attachments referenced: MedSpec_QPS_and_Retention_Sheet.xlsx
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Chris Moore <chris@medspec.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot -> Prod migration ask: handoff runbook and credits

Thanks Chris — great to see this moving forward.

We're attaching a concise migration playbook that our Solutions Engineering team uses for pilot handoffs (MedSpec_Migration_Playbook_v1.pdf). It covers canary windows, traffic ramp, instrumentation hooks, and rollback decision gates. High level responses to your asks below:

- Migration playbook: yes, attached. Includes recommended canary cadence (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 72 hours) and specific alert thresholds for quality drift and token-level latency.
- Rollback credits: we can offer a conditional crediting mechanism for a short period, subject to agreed rollback triggers and smoke-test criteria. I'll loop Ben (pricing) to propose a concrete credit structure.
- Feature/tier constraints: we recommend pinning model version and not changing quantization or batching profiles during the canary. Tier swaps (e.g., compact -> core) can be staged but need coordination with Dedicated capacity if you use reserved pools.

Can you confirm the target date for the handoff window and whether you expect Dedicated capacity or hosted API? Once we have that, Ben will share a proposed credit schedule and Lauren will prepare a draft amendment if needed.

Cheers,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Thu, Aug 26, 2026 at 10:12 AM Chris Moore <chris@medspec.ai> wrote:
> Hi Priya,
>
> Thanks again for the pilot guidance...
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Chris Moore <chris@medspec.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-27T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot -> Prod migration ask: handoff runbook and credits

Hi Chris, Priya — looping in pricing to propose options.

Short proposal (we can formalize with an amendment):
- Conditional rollback credit: 60% of equivalent monthly committed spend applied as one-time credit if a rollback occurs within the first 60 days AND the rollback meets two of three pre-agreed failure gates (data leak, >15% quality regression on evals, or systemic latency breach >150% of baseline).
- Canary protection: we can provide a temporary buffer (grace capacity) for the first 14 days to absorb traffic spikes tied to the migration at no additional charge (up to 2x your baseline throughput), capped at a pre-agreed ceiling.
- Tier swap coordination: if you move from a Compact to Core tier during handoff, we recommend a 48-hour stale-KV warmup window; we will not bill tier-delta for the warmup period if it is explicitly called out in the amendment.

If that sounds reasonable I can drop a draft amendment and a DocuSign link. Also attaching the pricing worksheet we used to model this (see MedSpec_QPS_and_Retention_Sheet.xlsx).

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On Thu, Aug 26, 2026 at 1:45 PM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Chris — great to see this moving forward...
From: Chris Moore <chris@medspec.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta@medspec.ai>
Date: 2026-08-27T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot -> Prod migration ask: handoff runbook and credits

Ben — appreciate the detailed offer. A couple quick clarifications:

- The 60% credit: is that relative to our committed monthly spend or a committed pilot baseline? We plan to sign a 6-month reserved capacity next week but would want the rollback credit to apply against the first two months of that commit if triggered.
- The 14-day grace capacity sounds great — can we request that the ceiling be set to 3x baseline for the first 48 hours only (we expect an initial spike when routing goes live)?

If we can get those two items clarified in the amendment, we're comfortable proceeding with a canary starting 2026-09-07. Also would like a short 30-minute runbook walkthrough with your SRE lead on 2026-09-03.

Thanks —
Chris

On Fri, Aug 27, 2026 at 9:10 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Chris, Priya — looping in pricing to propose options...
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot -> Prod migration ask: handoff runbook and credits

Chris, team — thanks for the quick sync and concrete asks. Priya/Bob (SRE), please schedule the 30-minute runbook walkthrough on Sept 3; Ben/legal/finance will update the amendment with the two clarifications:

- Credit basis: apply to first two months of the committed reserved capacity (60% credit as described) if rollback is triggered per gates.
- Grace capacity: we will honor up to 3x baseline for the initial 48 hours, then revert to 2x cap for the remainder of the 14-day window.

I've attached a draft amendment (Draft_MigrationCredit_Amendment.docx) and opened the DocuSign envelope for signature (link below). Please review and provide redlines by EOD 2026-08-31 so legal can finalize.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
